title: Japan Needs Higher Interest Rates
gist: Only a teaser is available: Hamada argues that while easing was right in 2012 amid deflation, today's weak yen and higher US rates call for much tighter Japanese monetary policy.

insights.claim: Japan's weak yen combined with higher US interest rates calls for a much tighter monetary policy, the opposite of the 2012 deflation-era stance.
insights.speaker: KOICHI HAMADA
insights.so_what: Supports a bias toward further BoJ tightening and yen strength.
insights.quote: Japan faces the opposite problem: a weak yen, combined with higher interest rates in the US, calls for a much tighter monetary policy.

insights.claim: Policymakers were right to embrace monetary easing, including lower interest rates, in 2012 when Japan faced chronic deflation.
insights.speaker: KOICHI HAMADA
insights.so_what: Regime change: the easing rationale no longer applies.

insights.claim: The cheap yen (yen yasu) has been hard on Japan's economy even as it draws tourists with favorable exchange rates and low prices such as roughly $20 restaurant lunches.
insights.speaker: KOICHI HAMADA
insights.so_what: Weak-yen tourism boom masks domestic purchasing-power costs.
